source.title: A survey detection channel overrides the pixels in an astronomical foundation model, and biases tomographic mean redshifts

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether sparse dictionaries provide reliable causal handles on a model behavior. Its results refine or challenge the idea that dictionary features are stable, useful units: steering varies substantially across dictionaries and seeds, and usually loses to simpler baselines.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the superposition hypothesis but does not test feature superposition, capacity competition, or feature geometry. Its image-token brightness-ladder and codebook findings are not results about superposed directions. The sparse-dictionary steering results in Section 7 and Table 8 bear on V5; the paper does not test whether SAE features are complete representations or canonical units.
record.test_reason: Section 7 and Table 8 train 15 SAEs on block-6 activations of aion-base. They vary width, k and seed, and run each through the same matched-norm causal steering test. Seed-to-seed spread and reconstruction–steering decoupling bear indirectly on V5's claim that dictionary features are stable, canonical units. The test measures steering utility of selected directions, not feature identity across seeds. The model is not an LLM and nothing tests superposition geometry, so V1–V4 and V6 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that SAEs reconstruct far better than PCA (FVU 0.032 vs 0.242) yet are unreliable causal handles. They add that single-seed causal evaluations of dictionaries are uninformative, because the seed spread exceeds the claimed effect. The SAE section is a minor part of a paper mainly about AION-1's detection-gate systematic.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of Toy Models of Superposition. It evaluates sparse-dictionary steering on an astronomical foundation model, rather than testing superposition geometry in toy networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dictionary width, sparsity k, and random seed alter recovery; at fixed width and sparsity, seed changes recovery by up to 18.4 percentage points. The sweep is at block 6 and uses α = 4 at matched intervention norm.

fits_no_version.finding: In a non-LLM astronomy transformer, a BatchTopK SAE (8192, k=32) reconstructs block-6 activations at FVU 0.032 versus 0.242 for PCA at matched k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionaries recover structure better than PCA in non-language foundation models (V4-like, outside LLMs).

fits_no_version.finding: A difference-in-means gate direction recovers 46% of the collapse versus 5% for random at α=4. Per-object directions agree only to 0.80, and 22 of 768 dimensions capture 90% of the remainder.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learned 'source present' gate is only partly carried by one direction (bears on 1-D vs multi-dimensional representation, not on superposition).

record.problems: Evidence on V5 is limited to causal steering utility for one model family, one layer, and one target behavior. The authors state that dictionary training is not bit-reproducible and that the observed seed spread includes run-to-run nondeterminism as well as seed variance. The dictionary arm is described as the paper's noisiest measurement. This does not test completeness or canonicality of the features.

untested.parts: Completeness of SAE features. Canonicality or feature matching across seeds and widths. Stability measured on the features themselves rather than on steering recovery. Any layer other than block 6. Features chosen by causal effect rather than activation gap.
Not tested in LLMs. SAE reconstruction is reported only for an astronomy foundation model.
Not tested. The brightness ladder concerns tokeniser codes, not superposed model features.

missing.what: Per-dictionary FVU, alive-feature %, and PCA FVU at the same k. Best reconstructor (FVU 0.023) recovers 53.5%; best steerer has FVU 0.067 and 10.5% alive. This is the decoupling of reconstruction and causal utility.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence on V5 is indirect: it concerns causal steering utility of activation-gap-selected entries at one layer of one non-LLM model. The authors note that seed spread includes hardware nondeterminism. Hence limits_scope rather than challenges. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Not tested; the study does not measure feature spreading across neurons or SAE recovery of features in LLMs.
Tests causal steering utility and its variation across dictionary configurations and seeds. Does not establish whether SAE features are complete representations or canonical units.
The paper reports a one-dimensional brightness ladder in image-token codes, not whether superposed model features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Fixed width and k=32, seeds 0/1/2 (aion-base, block 6, α=4, matched norm)
relationships.reason: Recovery shifts with seed alone: 62.8/63.9/45.5% (r2, r10, r11), 31.5/26.0/34.2% (r5, r12, r13) and 54.2/69.7/52.2% (r8, r14, r15). Dictionaries do not yield stable causal handles, though the spread partly reflects non-bit-reproducible training.
relationships.display_finding: With width and k fixed, recovery across seeds 0, 1 and 2 was 62.8/63.9/45.5%, 31.5/26.0/34.2% and 54.2/69.7/52.2% in three settings, though non-bit-reproducible training explains part of the spread.

source_check.condition: Fixed width and k=32, seeds 0/1/2 (aion-base, block 6, α=4, matched norm)
source_check.reason: r2,r10,r11,r5,r12,r13,r8,r14,r15 correctly report variable recovery, but no individual-feature correspondence or identity stability is measured. The text also attributes spread partly to training nondeterminism. Stability of downstream steering is distinct from V5's stability of representational units.

relationships.reason: Recovery ranges 31.5–74.7% across configurations (r1–r9). All beat the random control (13.4%), but only one beats matched-k PCA. Usefulness of dictionary directions depends on hyperparameter choice, and per the text, not on reconstruction quality.
relationships.display_finding: Recovery ranged 31.5–74.7% across configurations; all beat the 13.4% random control but only one beat matched-k PCA, and usefulness did not track reconstruction quality.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: r1–r9 establish hyperparameter-sensitive causal utility and reconstruction–steering decoupling. V5 does not assert that activation-gap-selected steering directions outperform PCA or difference-in-means; completeness, stability and canonicality remain untested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study applies SAE dictionaries as an interpretability tool. Its steering-performance comparison addresses a related construct rather than any listed version's representational claim.

tranche.reason: Section 7 uses sparse dictionaries to construct steering directions and benchmarks their causal utility. It does not measure dictionary completeness or match individual features across seeds or widths; these performance results do not test V5 as written.

source_check.notes: All listed recovery values, baselines, models and conditions match Section 7 and Table 8. The authors' causal-utility conclusion is accurately paraphrased; it should remain separate from claims about canonical feature identity.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: The 15 tested SAE dictionaries at α = 4, with the reported matched-norm causal steering setup
reader_labels.reason: Dictionary recovery spans 26.0–74.7%; only two of fifteen beat difference-in-means, and seed changes at fixed width and sparsity reach 18.4 percentage points, challenging stability as a causal feature handle (r1–r15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Configurations where SAE directions recover some gate-induced collapse
reader_labels.reason: All 15 dictionaries beat the random control and dictionary directions carry signal, but the study does not show that this makes them complete or canonical representation units (r1–r15, r17).
